svg.text: Keritot 13b: three readings of Leviticus 10:9 in the baraita
“Intoxicating drink” is wine, learned by verbal analogy from the nazirite.
Forbidden only enough to intoxicate: a quarter-log of wine forty days old.
“Wine” teaches it is prohibited in any amount and from its press.
Rashi: for those, a warning but not death.
“Intoxicating drink” is other intoxicating beverages; he does not learn from the nazirite.
“Wine”: for wine, death at the hand of Heaven; for other drinks, a prohibition.
The baraita of the Ke’ila fig, honey or milk (he is flogged) follows him.
“Wine…and intoxicating drink”: do not drink it in the manner that it intoxicates.
If he interrupted, or put in any amount of water, he is exempt.
Halakha like Rabbi Elazar (Rav Yehuda bar Aḥotai; Rav)
Rav Ashi: that is with a quarter-log; he himself had drunk more than a quarter-log.
